h1: Metal shears — hydraulic and mechanical shears, 20 ga to 1-9/16″
intro: A metal shear (sheet metal shearing machine, guillotine shear, shear cutter) cuts plate and sheet to size in one stroke between a fixed bottom blade and a top blade on the moving beam — the first machine in every sheet-metal, HVAC, signage and fabrication shop, before the press brake. NovoTech sells two kinds in Canada, each on its own page: hydraulic shears — swing beam and variable-rake guillotine plate shears to 1-9/16″ and 26 ft, in a premium line made in Turkey and a value line built to our specification, and light hydraulic shears from 16 ga to 1/4″ for the sheet-metal shop; and mechanical shears, with no hydraulics at all — direct-gear SRGM guillotines for 1/8″ and 1/4″ at 31 to 35 strokes a minute, electric and NC electric shears, motorized bench shears and a coil slitting and cut-to-length machine. Below, the two kinds compared and the questions we get asked; every machine comes with a CSA-approved panel, a 1-year warranty and installation, training and parts from Mississauga, ON, Canada.
hero_points: Hydraulic: swing beam 5/32″ – 3/4″ × 6.8 – 20 ft and guillotine 1/4″ – 1-9/16″ × 8 – 26 ft; premium BS / BSY and DAS CNC, value QC12K / Q11K; light hydraulic shears 16 ga – 1/4″
Mechanical: SRGM direct-gear guillotines 1/8″ × 3.6 – 10 ft and 1/4″ × 3.6 – 13.8 ft, 31 – 35 strokes/min
Electric and NC electric shears 14 ga – 5/32″ × 49 – 100″, motorized bench shears and a 48″ coil slitting and cut-to-length machine

faq.q: Hydraulic or mechanical shear — which should I buy?
faq.a: By the material and the hours. For sheet to 14 ga in a sheet-metal, HVAC or signage shop, the lowest-priced powered machines are the motorized bench shears, the Q11 electric shears and the light hydraulic shears, 26″ to 120″. For 1/8″ and 1/4″ all day, a mechanical guillotine shear is the faster and simpler machine: direct-gear drive, 31 – 35 strokes a minute, no hydraulics, with return-to-sender and cut-to-length versions. From 1/4″ plate up — 3/8″, 1/2″, to 1-9/16″ over 20 and 26 ft — the hydraulic shears are the machines, swing beam for the everyday plate shear and a variable-rake guillotine for production and thick plate. A mechanical shear has no hydraulic power pack, no oil to heat up and no valves or seals to service, and cuts the same on the first and the thousandth stroke; a small hydraulic shear is the quietest way to cut 14 ga to 5/32″ a few times an hour. Each kind comes in a premium and a value line on its page, and every machine is installed and supported by the same NovoTech technicians.

The premium hydraulic shears (Dener BS / BSY and DAS CNC) and mechanical shears (SRGM) are built in Turkey on the heaviest frames with European hydraulics, motors and controls and parts in Mississauga, ON, Canada — for two shifts a day and the tightest cut. NovoTech's value line — the QC12K / Q11K hydraulic shears with Estun controls, the light hydraulic shears and the electric, bench and coil machines — is built in China to our specification at about two-thirds of the price, the right buy for a job shop. Both lines are sections on each page, so the comparison is side by side.

On a swing beam shear the beam pivots on two bearings and the cylinders swing it through the cut — few parts, a low price and a rake angle fixed by the design, which is fine for plate. A guillotine shear carries the beam straight down on rollers with a variable rake angle, so the same machine cuts thin sheet flat and fast at a small angle and thick plate at a steeper one; it also keeps the blade gap set automatically. For a plate shop cutting mostly 3/8″ and up, a swing beam shear (Dener BS, NovoTech QC12K); for a job shop that cuts everything from 16 ga to 3/4″ and beyond, a guillotine (Dener DAS, NovoTech Q11K).

faq.q: How is the capacity rated, and what about stainless and aluminum?
faq.a: Capacities are the makers' ratings for mild steel (about 65,000 psi) over the full blade length. Stainless steel is harder to shear, so count on about 60 % of the mild-steel thickness — 14 ga stainless on a 1/8″ machine, 11 ga on a 1/4″ machine, 3/8″ on a 5/8″ machine; aluminum cuts to the full rated thickness and about 50 % more. Tell us your thickest material and we size the shear with a margin.

The model number is the maximum shearing length in millimetres: 1250 – 1360 = 49 – 53.5″ (a 4 × 8 sheet cut across), 1500 – 1560 = 5 ft, 2000 – 2060 = 6.6 – 6.8 ft, 2500 – 2560 = 8.2 – 8.4 ft (a 4 × 8 sheet lengthwise), 3000 – 3200 = 10 – 10.5 ft (5 × 10 sheet), 4000 = 13 ft, 6000 = 20 ft plate. Most sheet-metal shops run an 8 or 10 ft machine so a full sheet is cut both ways; HVAC and signage shops are well served by 52 – 81″; plate shops buy 10 to 20 ft.

faq.q: What is the back gauge, and is it NC?
faq.a: The back gauge is the stop behind the blade that sets the width of the cut strip. The value-line light hydraulic and electric shears have a manual gauge with counter, an electric gauge or a PLC-positioned gauge depending on the model; the SRGM and the hydraulic plate shears come with an NC back gauge — the operator keys in the dimension and the gauge moves there — and the Dener DAS with a 1 m ball-screw gauge set by the CNC together with the blade gap and the cutting angle.

faq.q: What about safety and the Ontario pre-start review?
faq.a: Finger guards along the blade, rear guard fences or photocells / light curtains, an anti-repeat single-stroke control and a mobile foot pedal with emergency stop are standard or available on every line; we recommend the photocell or light-curtain rear guard on every powered shear. In Ontario a new shear needs a pre-start health and safety review (PSR) under Regulation 851 before it runs.

faq.q: Do you deliver, install and service in Canada?
faq.a: Yes — every shear is shipped to Mississauga, ON, Canada, unloaded, levelled, commissioned and the operators trained by NovoTech; blades and parts for all four lines are stocked here. Every machine comes with a CSA-approved panel, 600 V standard (208 / 240 / 480 V on request) and a 1-year warranty.

faq.q: What voltage do these machines run on?
faq.a: Three-phase machines are supplied for 600 V as standard with a CSA-approved panel; 208 V, 240 V and 480 V 3-phase are available on request, and 240 V single-phase on models whose main motor is 2.2 kW (3 HP) or less — a machine with a motor above 2.2 kW must run on three-phase power and cannot be converted to 240 V single-phase. Manual machines have no electrics.
